title: Ephemeral probe orchestrator and handoff guardrails for interactive oncall diagnostics
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: During recent oncall war rooms we repeatedly ran short-lived probes (service health, grpc call probes, trace pulls) ad-hoc via the incident bot, but lacked coordination, cost control, and safe handoff semantics. This PR implements an Ephemeral Probe Orchestrator (EPO) for interactive diagnostics and a set of handoff guardrails to make probes repeatable, auditable, and safe to run during a shift change. Summary of changes: 1) orchestrator service (incident-bot/probes) - new lightweight orchestrator that schedules ephemeral probes with time-to-live, scoped credentials, and automatic artifact collection; 2) probe playbooks - a curated set of probe templates (http/health, grpc-ping, trace-sampler, metrics-snapshot) that include cost/side-effect metadata; 3) handoff guardrails - checksum-based artifact manifests and a two-step "snapshot and handoff" flow that validates artifacts before transferring to the next oncall; 4) CLI/Slack actions - interactive slash command updates for starting probes, viewing in-progress probes, and attaching artifacts to the incident thread; 5) safety and privacy - automatic PII redaction in logs, rate-limits, and a dry-run permission check; 6) observability - per-probe tracing, metrics (duration, bytes, error-rate), and a lightweight probe dashboard. Checklist: - [x] Core orchestrator implementation + scheduler - [x] Probe templates and templating engine - [x] Slack command + ephemeral tokens - [x] Manifest checksum and handoff flow - [x] Safety gating and RBAC checks - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Documentation and runbook update Commits (high-level): - Initial scaffold of probes service and protobufs - Add templating for probe run definitions and TTL enforcement - Wire Slack actions and ephemeral tokens; add CLI commands - Implement artifact manifest, checksum algorithm (SHA256), and handoff API - Add PII scrubber and incorporate rate-limit guards - Tests: unit tests for scrubber, integration tests for probe lifecycle - Docs: runbook and quickstart in docs/oncall/probes.md Changed areas (high level): - incident-bot/cmd/probes/ (new orchestrator binary)
- incident-bot/internal/probes/
- incident-bot/internal/scrubbers/pii.go
- incident-bot/web/handlers/probe_api.go
- incident-bot/slack/commands/probe_command.go
- docs/oncall/probes.md
- tests/integration/probes_lifecycle_test.go Review conversation summary: - Priya: requested that manifests include a minimal provenance block (who started probe, linear id, correlation id). Author response: added provenance fields and included them in the manifest (commit 4). - Evan: flagged concern about burst probe storms; asked for an adaptive semaphore and cost estimator. Author response: implemented a lightweight in-memory semaphore with cost budget heuristics and a per-incident cap; added metrics and alerts to detect bursts. - Liam: wanted stronger defaults for PII scrubbing and an escape hatch for advanced debugging. Author response: default scrubber is conservative; added an explicit "allow-raw" flag gated by RBAC for Platform SREs only. CI and checks: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: one flaky probe timing test failed on first run; flake fixed by stabilizing test timeouts - Lint: gofmt/golangci-lint passed - Security scan: no high severity findings Merge: squash and merge after approvals (2 approvals) and green CI. Release notes: "Add Ephemeral Probe Orchestrator: run safe, short-lived diagnostics during incidents; includes handoff manifest and built-in PII scrubbing. Admin-only option to allow raw artifacts."

notes_for_release: Introduces Ephemeral Probe Orchestrator (interactive oncall probes). Default behavior scrubs PII; raw artifacts require admin RBAC. Adds probe metrics and a runbook in docs/oncall/probes.md.
